frame: possessive attractor on the main verb: the [pl]' [sg] ___
decider_quote: "was printed" (past starting point, in "from the season it was printed", 7+ words after the blank) and "borrow" (present, continuing)

distractor_kills.have been indispensable: number: subject "questionnaire" (head of the subject NP, ~3 words before the blank); "statisticians'" is a possessive. Correct in: "The statisticians have been indispensable to planners from the start."
distractor_kills.are indispensable: number ("questionnaire") + aspect: simple present cannot take "from the season it was printed" (7-12 words after the blank). Correct in: "The statisticians' notes are indispensable to planners."
distractor_kills.is indispensable: aspect only: "from the season it was printed" (words 7-12 after the blank) sets a past starting point that the simple present cannot reach back to; "borrow" shows the state continuing. Correct in: "The questionnaire is indispensable to planners today."

hostile_reader.options_only_pick: none: clean 2x2 has been/have been/is/are + shared complement; no extra word; key not uniquely longest or shortest
heuristics_that_give_key: (b) loosely: plural possessor 2 words before the blank -> sg (correct)
hostile_reader.changed: moved "from the season it was printed" from word 4 to word 7 after the blank (it decides aspect, so it may not sit within 4 words); replaced "nearly every" with "nearly all of its" to avoid the "every" trap phrase

frame: second verb of a compound predicate, far from its subject: The Xs V ... and ___
decider_quote: "transcribed" (the first predicate, simple and completed) and "stopped accepting entries two winters ago" (next sentence)

distractor_kills.has been contributing: number (subject "teachers", ~15 words before the blank) + progressive ("stopped accepting entries two winters ago", next sentence). Correct in: "The museum has been contributing to the registry each month."
distractor_kills.has contributed: number only: the subject of both predicates is "teachers" at the start of the sentence, ~15 words before the blank; "schoolmistress" is inside the first predicate's object. Correct in: "The schoolmistress's family has contributed to the registry."
distractor_kills.have been contributing: progressive only: registries that "stopped accepting entries two winters ago" (next sentence, 7+ words after the blank) cannot still be receiving contributions; parallel with completed "transcribed". Correct in: "Volunteers have been contributing to the open registry all month."

hostile_reader.options_only_pick: none: clean 2x2 has/have x V-en/been V-ing, one verb; key not uniquely longest or shortest
heuristics_that_give_key: (a) opposite of the noun before the blank (sg -> pl, correct)
hostile_reader.changed: dropped the number word "Two" from the subject (C1 and C6 also opened with "Two ...": shared topic shape)

frame: whose-relative: singular antecedent, whose + plural noun as the clause subject
decider_quote: "kept" (first sentence), "wrote" and "never attended" (frame sentence, 6+ words after the blank), "memorized" and "burned" (last sentence)

distractor_kills.was being passed: number: clause subject "scripts" immediately before the blank; "playwright" is the main-clause subject. Correct in: "The playwright's only script was being passed hand to hand."
distractor_kills.is being passed: number ("scripts", adjacent) + tense ("wrote", "never attended", 6+ words after; "kept" in the previous sentence). Correct in: "The new script is being passed around the cast today."
distractor_kills.are being passed: tense only: past narrative ("kept" previous sentence; "wrote", "never attended" 6-10 words after the blank; "memorized", "burned" next sentence). Correct in: "Copies of the script are being passed around the cast this week."

hostile_reader.options_only_pick: cannot pick: all four carry "being"; but the key "were being passed" is the uniquely longest option (1 of my 2 allowed)
heuristics_that_give_key: none of a-g except the uniquely-longest tell, which the brief caps at 2 per author
hostile_reader.changed: after-blank continuation changed from a PP ("from cellar to cellar") to the adverbial "hand to hand" so that not every item is followed by a PP. RISK (table-imposed): Near = pl = key, so the adjacent "scripts" strikes both singular distractors from next to the blank; the misleader is the early antecedent only

frame: nonrestrictive , which ___ whose antecedent is the whole preceding clause
true_subject_head: which (= the clause "a conservator first strips the yellowed varnish left by earlier owners")
decider_quote: "Whenever a museum lends" and "strips" (habitual present frame), then "read", "compare", "goes" (next sentence)

distractor_kills.has been logged: aspect only: the frame is a recurring procedure ("Whenever a museum lends", start of the sentence; "read", "compare", "goes" in the next sentence), so the logging recurs with each loan rather than being one completed event. Correct in: "The treatment has been logged, so the crate can be sealed."
distractor_kills.are logged: number: "owners" cannot be logged "as a separate treatment" (words 4-7 after the blank); the antecedent is the stripping. Correct in: "The earlier owners are logged in the provenance file."
distractor_kills.have been logged: number + aspect (as above). Correct in: "All previous treatments have been logged."

hostile_reader.options_only_pick: none: clean 2x2; the key "is logged" is the uniquely shortest (1 of my 2 allowed)
heuristics_that_give_key: (a) opposite of noun before the blank (pl -> sg, correct)
hostile_reader.changed: chose "owners" (people) as the clause-final plural so that "which" cannot sensibly refer to it with "as a separate treatment"; an earlier draft ending in "watercolors" was rejected because "watercolors ... are" would be defensible. Exclusivity of perfect vs simple rests on the habitual frame: the weakest decision in my 8

frame: subject relative whose antecedent is the FAR plural across a PP: the Xs behind the Y that ___
decider_quote: "wears his everyday black cassock" (the priest is not in costume) and "sew the costumes" / "fit them onto the boys before dawn" (the grandmothers are the doers), both in the next sentence

distractor_kills.is dressing: number (priest "wears his everyday black cassock", next sentence) + voice (grandmothers "fit them onto the boys before dawn", next sentence). Correct in: "The priest is dressing for the service."
distractor_kills.are dressing: voice only: the grandmothers dress the boys, and do so "before dawn", so during the procession the boys are not putting costumes on themselves (next sentence, 12+ words after the blank). Correct in: "The boys are dressing as spirits in the back room."
distractor_kills.is dressed: number only: the clause cannot describe the priest, who "wears his everyday black cassock" (next sentence). Correct in: "The priest that is dressed in black leads the line."

hostile_reader.options_only_pick: none: clean 2x2, one verb; key not uniquely longest or shortest
heuristics_that_give_key: (a) opposite of noun before the blank (sg -> pl, correct)
hostile_reader.changed: rejected "regarded as" (both active options die locally because "regarding as" needs an object: two free strikes); chose ergative "dress as" so that the active is grammatical in the clause and is ruled out only by the next sentence; avoided a plural as-complement ("as spirits") because it would resolve number within 4 words

frame: unlike those of ... comparison phrase between subject and verb
decider_quote: "followed" (in "each of the seasons that followed its premiere", 13+ words after the blank) and "write" (present, continuing)

distractor_kills.is traveling: aspect only: present progressive cannot cover "each of the seasons that followed its premiere" (13+ words after the blank). Correct in: "This month the script is traveling to three towns."
distractor_kills.have been traveling: number: subject "script" (~12 words before the blank); "those" and "dramas" are inside the comparison phrase. Correct in: "The puppeteers have been traveling for weeks."
distractor_kills.are traveling: number + aspect (as above). Correct in: "The marionette dramas are traveling to the coast this week."

hostile_reader.options_only_pick: none: clean 2x2; ratio 1.5 but key not uniquely longest

frame: noun-complement (content) clause inside the subject: The claim that the Xs V ... ___
decider_quote: "never needed to promote it" and "spread by itself" (next sentence)

distractor_kills.was being circulated: voice only: the next sentence says nobody needed to promote it and it "spread by itself", so no one was circulating it. Correct in: "The pamphlet was being circulated by the abbey's rivals."
distractor_kills.were circulating: number: subject "claim" opens the sentence ~10 words before the blank; "monks" and "charters" are inside the that-clause. Correct in: "Copies of the charters were circulating among lawyers."
distractor_kills.were being circulated: number + voice. Correct in: "Forged copies were being circulated by a rival house."

hostile_reader.options_only_pick: none: clean 2x2; key "was circulating" uniquely shortest (2 of my 2 allowed)
hostile_reader.changed: "traveled by itself" -> "spread by itself" so no lexical verb repeats C6's key; "(d) no object -> passive" fails here by design

frame: fronted -ing participial phrase + inversion (Complicating ... ___ the ... Ys), plural postposed head 5+ words after the blank

distractor_kills.was the: number (head "initials", 5 words after the blank) + tense ("disagree", "read", "dismiss" in the neighbouring sentences). Correct in: "Complicating the sale was the owner's sudden death."
distractor_kills.is the: number only: postposed head "initials" is 5 words after the blank; "attempt", "panel", "master" are inside the fronted phrase. Correct in: "Complicating the attribution is the panel's missing frame."
distractor_kills.were the: tense only: the dispute is current ("disagree" before; "read", "dismiss" after). Correct in: "Complicating the first restoration were the earlier repairs."

heuristics_that_give_key: none of a-g (a gives sg: wrong)
